correctness.rationale: Reconstructed source quiver with u:S1->P1, v:P1->S1, b:P1->P3, a:P3->P1 using left-to-right path multiplication, taking care not to confuse map-composition order. At the interior shared tree edge the two special cycles are vu and ba; their weighted equality gives vu=(ba)^m. The cross-cycle type-III zero products are ub and av. Schroll Section 2.4 minimality criterion shows no further independent type-II relations for this path (the immediate successor at each truncation is not again truncated). In C_m, uv is a nonzero path; (uv)u=u(vu)=u(ba)^m=0 and v(uv)=(vu)v=(ba)^mv=0, with all other products ruled out by endpoints. Thus k uv is a two-sided 1-dimensional socle ideal. Basis lengths give dim C_m=4m+6, dim B_m=4m+5, agreeing with source basis. Every quotient module indecomposable over B_m is indecomposable over C_m, and the three-edge Brauer tree algebra is representation-finite; the conclusion holds for ALL m, not by finite tests.

final_claim: For each m>=1 over the algebraically closed base field, the Liu--Xin Example 6.3 algebra B_m=kQ/<uv,ub,av,vu-(ba)^m> (left-to-right paths) is C_m/<uv>, where C_m=kQ/<ub,av,vu-(ba)^m> is the three-edge path Brauer tree algebra (interior multiplicities 1,m); uv spans a one-dimensional socle ideal; every B_m is representation-finite.
limitations: Only Liu--Xin Example 6.3 family m>=1; no claim on arbitrary endomorphism algebras outside the G-condition.
Representation-finiteness is a theorem from the tree cover, not an independently enumerated indecomposable classification.
